lens: Numerical-methods expert: numerical stability of the change transform, quantization-error propagation, and drift elimination by construction

proposals.name: P1 — Closed-loop asinh-domain integer delta grid (rank 1: highest robustness x simplicity; eliminates ALL offset heuristics, epsilon, and anchors)
proposals.mechanism: Replace percent-change + cumprod with: (a) per-variable transform y_i[t] = asinh(x_i[t]/s_i), where s_i > 0 is a per-variable scale stored in metadata; (b) quantize the TRANSFORM VALUES to an integer lattice m_i[t] = round(y_i[t]/q_i) with per-variable step q_i (this IS the adaptive quantization); (c) the grid pixel is the integer delta k_i[t] = m_i[t] - m_i[t-1], offset to uint8 as k+128 (uint16 as k+32768). Decode: m = m0 + cumsum(k); x̂ = s·sinh(q·m). I verified numerically that this integer-diff form is EXACTLY equivalent to closed-loop DPCM with a previous-value predictor and mid-tread quantizer: because reconstruction is integer accumulation of integer codes, cumsum(diff(m)) == m identically, so |ŷ[t]-y[t]| <= q/2 for ALL t — verified at 1.5M steps, max error 0.00200 with q/2 = 0.002, zero drift. Deltas exceeding the 8-bit range (|k|>127) are escape-coded: clip in the grid, store exact (var,t,k) triples int32 in a zstd side list, so the bound survives clipping. asinh is odd, monotone, defined on all of R: negatives and zero-crossings need NO offset, NO epsilon, NO sign bookkeeping — dy/dx = 1/sqrt(x^2+s^2) is log-like for |x|>>s (percent-change spirit: equal quantization steps = equal relative changes) and linear for |x|<s (graceful absolute coding near zero, exactly where percent-change blows up). Setting s_i small approaches pure log/relative coding; s_i large approaches pure affine/absolute coding — one parameter spans the whole abs↔rel continuum. Error bound is user-specifiable per point: given relative tolerance rho and absolute floor a, set s_i = a/rho and q_i = 2·asinh-domain rho; guaranteed |x̂-x| <= sinh(q/2)·sqrt(s_i^2 + x̂^2), i.e. rel err <= ~q/2 for |x|>s, abs err <= ~s·q/2 near zero (verified empirically: 0.00515 vs q/2=0.005, 5.06e-5 vs 5e-5).
proposals.why_it_wins: Root cause of both catastrophic failure modes is open-loop cumprod: per-step quantization errors multiply, so error grows unboundedly (MetroPT-3 RMSE 3.8e95) and the offset/anchor machinery exists only to paper over it. Closed-loop integer accumulation makes error NON-ACCUMULATING BY CONSTRUCTION — the T-step reconstruction has the same q/2 bound as a 1-step one. Information-theoretically this also fixes the rate side: the code alphabet is the integer increment k, whose distribution is the quantized asinh-increment — sharply Laplacian and zero-centered, unlike the current mu-law output which deliberately spreads codes over the full [0,255] range and leaves PNG DEFLATE nothing to exploit. Measured on a Laplacian random walk at q yielding max err 0.002: H(k) = 4.77 bits/px → ratio ~0.075 vs float64 before container gains, with entropy falling further on real quasi-stationary sensor data. It also delivers the missing feature vs SZ3/ZFP: a guaranteed per-point mixed abs/rel error bound (failure mode 5). Anchors become pure random-access aids, not accuracy patches, and auto_offset/near_zero_std_factor/epsilon are deleted outright.
proposals.expected_gain: MetroPT-3 (1.5M steps): divergence eliminated categorically — unanchored RMSE goes from 3.8e95 to the q-determined bound; expect RMSE ~1 at ratio ~0.02 (current anchored: 1.71 @ 0.0297, and the 64-bit-float anchor stream disappears). UCI Air Quality: current Enh 8b+Anchors RMSE 108.3 @ 0.114; with per-variable q at rho=0.5% and s_i ≈ 0.05·sigma_i, expect RMSE ~0.5–5 (channel RMS is O(10^2–10^3)) at ratio 0.06–0.10 — a 20–200x RMSE reduction at BETTER ratio. Honest caveat: this alone lands TRACQ on ZFP's rate-distortion curve at low rates (<= 8 bits/value) rather than dominating it at ZFP's 17-bit operating point (0.004 @ 0.273); dominating needs P3's sparsity on top. 16-bit mode with rho=0.005% reaches RMSE ~0.005–0.05 at ratio ~0.15–0.22, directly comparable to ZFP tol=1e-1.
proposals.implementation_sketch: New class ClosedLoopGrid in tracq/core_enhanced.py (~120 lines), same quantize_8bit/quantize_16bit/reconstruct_from_quantized API so codec.py and container.py work unchanged. Encode: s = np.maximum(np.median(np.abs(x),axis=1)*s_frac, abs_floor) (or s=a/rho from user tolerances); y = np.arcsinh(x/s[:,None]); m = np.round(y/q[:,None]).astype(np.int64); k = np.diff(m,axis=1); esc = np.abs(k)>127; escapes = np.argwhere(esc) plus k[esc] as int32 arrays (zstd, into metadata side channel); grid = (np.clip(k,-127,127)+128).astype(np.uint8); store m[:,0] (int64), s, q in metadata. Decode: k = grid.astype(np.int64)-128; k[esc_idx] = esc_val; m = np.concatenate([m0[:,None], m0[:,None]+np.cumsum(k,axis=1)],axis=1); x̂ = s[:,None]*np.sinh(q[:,None]*m). Choose per-variable q either from a user error bound (q=2rho) or rate-targeted: binary-search q_i so that the 99.9th percentile of |diff(round(y/q))| <= 127 (keeps escapes <0.1%). No sequential loop anywhere; no numba needed. Benchmark by adding one method row to scripts/realworld_benchmark.py and rate_distortion.py.
proposals.risk: (1) RMSE-metric mismatch: asinh at small s gives a RELATIVE bound, but the paper's headline metric is RMSE (absolute), which is dominated by the largest-magnitude samples — a relative-bound coder spends error budget exactly where RMSE punishes it. Mitigation is built in: for RMSE benchmarks set s_i ≈ sigma_i (mostly-affine regime, still asinh-protected against outliers); report both bounds. (2) Escape-list blowup on genuinely chaotic channels (H(k) → 8 bits, entropy stage gains nothing) — detect via per-variable H(k) estimate and fall back to 16-bit for that variable. (3) sinh overflow if q·m is huge — impossible in practice since |y| = |asinh(x/s)| <= ~40 for float64 inputs, but assert it.
proposals.interactions: This is the FOUNDATION the other mechanisms plug into: higher-order predictors become integer operations on m (k2 = diff(m,2), delta-of-delta ala Gorilla) with the same drift-free guarantee; the entropy stage (P3) requires the zero-centered sparse k alphabet this produces; anchors reduce to storing m[t] (int64) every A steps for O(1) random access, costing ~0.04 bits/value instead of float64s. Conflicts: mu-law companding and clamp-percentile machinery are superseded and should be deleted, not composed — companding a signal that is then closed-loop-quantized breaks the error bound.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Grid stays exactly (n_vars x n_time-1), one pixel per variable per timestep, uint8/uint16 PNG via the existing ImageCodec. Pixel 128 = no change; brightness deviation = signed relative-change magnitude — arguably MORE inspectable than the mu-law percent grid because drift-free semantics make the image a faithful 'derivative heatmap': anomalies are isolated bright/dark pixels, regime shifts are texture changes, and identical changes always map to identical gray levels across the whole series.

proposals.name: P2 — Affine per-variable normalization + closed-loop absolute integer deltas (rank 2: maximum simplicity, marginally weaker fidelity to the relative-change spirit)
proposals.mechanism: Same closed-loop integer machinery as P1 but with the identity transform on standardized data: z_i[t] = (x_i[t] - mu_i)/sigma_i, m = round(z/q_i), pixel = diff(m)+128. Reconstruction x̂ = mu + sigma·q·m. Guaranteed absolute per-point bound |x̂-x| <= sigma_i·q_i/2, uniform over the series. 'Relative change' survives as change-per-sigma: the grid still shows each variable's step normalized by its own scale, so cross-variable comparability — the visual point of the percent grid — is retained.
proposals.why_it_wins: It is the order-1-predictor core of what SZ3 actually does (Lorenzo predictor + error-bounded linear quantization + entropy coding), which the paper's own benchmarks show dominating TRACQ by 3–5 orders of magnitude — evidence this formulation, not percent-change, is the right substrate. It removes every division by signal values: no epsilon, no offsets, no clamp blending, no sign handling; robustness is unconditional for any finite float input. Its absolute error bound is exactly what the RMSE benchmark rewards (see P1 risk). Note P2 is the s_i → large limit of P1 (asinh linear regime) plus mean-centering, so shipping P1's code with a per-variable s-selection rule gets P2 for free.
proposals.expected_gain: Identical drift elimination to P1 (MetroPT-3 RMSE 3.8e95 → bounded). On near-Gaussian sensor channels (most of UCI Air Quality) it matches P1; on heavy-tailed/multi-decade channels it wastes levels on small values and P1 wins by ~1–2 bits/px at equal RMSE. Concretely: 8-bit grid, q at sigma/500 → per-point abs err <= sigma/1000, RMSE per channel ~sigma/1700 (uniform err) — for Air Quality sigma O(100–1000) that is RMSE ~0.06–0.6 at ratio ~0.08–0.11, versus current 108.3 @ 0.114. This is the single highest robustness-per-line-of-code change available.
proposals.implementation_sketch: Same ClosedLoopGrid class as P1 with transform='affine': subtract per-variable median (more robust than mean), divide by IQR-based sigma, then the identical round/diff/escape/cumsum path. ~15 extra lines over P1: store mu_i, sigma_i in metadata instead of s_i. Because it shares P1's code path, benchmark both from one implementation via the s/transform knob in scripts/rate_distortion.py.
proposals.risk: Weaker rate-distortion than P1 on channels whose natural error model is relative (flow rates, concentrations spanning decades): uniform absolute steps over-resolve the top of the range. A single extreme outlier inflates sigma if computed naively — use robust scale (IQR or MAD), which is 2 numpy calls. Loses the literal 'percent change' narrative for the paper; must be argued as 'scale-relative change', which reviewers may push on.
proposals.interactions: Free byproduct of P1's implementation (one branch). Same synergies with P3 sparsity and integer higher-order predictors. Supersedes auto_offset, adaptive clamp-percentile blending, and mu-law identically to P1.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Identical grid geometry and PNG path to P1; pixel = standardized-change intensity centered at 128. Cross-variable visual comparability is arguably improved because every row is in sigma units.

proposals.name: P3 — Dead-zone quantization with carried residual (rank 3: the ratio multiplier; needs P1/P2 underneath)
proposals.mechanism: On top of the P1/P2 closed loop, enlarge the quantizer's zero bin: emit k=0 whenever the accumulated transform-domain residual |y[t] - q·m̂[t-1]| < tau·q (tau in [0.5, 2]), else emit the mid-tread code. Because the loop is closed, the un-coded residual is NOT lost — it carries forward in the encoder's state and is emitted as soon as it crosses the threshold, so the worst-case per-point error is tau·q instead of q/2, still uniformly bounded, still zero drift. The grid becomes overwhelmingly the single value 128 on quiet stretches, which PNG's Up filter turns into zero runs and DEFLATE/Zstd crush to well under 0.5 bits/px. tau=0.5 is the plain mid-tread quantizer and costs nothing; tau>0.5 breaks the vectorized round-then-diff identity and needs a sequential scan — use the numba path already feature-flagged in this repo (HAS_NUMBA in core_enhanced.py), with a pure-numpy chunked fallback.
proposals.why_it_wins: This attacks failure mode 3 (lossy TRACQ barely beats lossless Delta+Zstd). The current pipeline creates no sparsity: mu-law intentionally fills [0,255]. Real sensor data is quasi-stationary — on MetroPT-3 the vast majority of steps are below any reasonable tolerance, so the entropy of the dead-zoned k stream approaches the burst rate. This is precisely the mechanism (error-bounded quantization → sparse integer codes → entropy coder) behind SZ3's ratios; TRACQ currently has the quantizer but throws away the sparsity before the entropy stage sees it.
proposals.expected_gain: MetroPT-3: expect >=80–95% of pixels to hit the zero bin at tolerances matching current anchored RMSE 1.71, driving ratio from ~0.03 to ~0.002–0.008 at equal or better RMSE — into genuine contention with PAA-1024 (1.55 @ 0.0007) while keeping per-timestep resolution, which PAA destroys (its actual differentiator for the rebuttal). Air Quality (noisier): 30–60% zeros, ratio improvement ~1.5–2.5x at fixed RMSE, e.g. 0.10 → 0.04–0.07. Combined with P1 this is what turns 'on ZFP's curve' into 'beats ZFP at the low-rate end'.
proposals.implementation_sketch: Extend ClosedLoopGrid.encode with tau parameter. numba kernel (~20 lines): for t in range(1,T): r = y[t] - q*m_prev; k = 0 if abs(r) < tau*q else round(r/q); m_prev += k; out[t-1] = k. Vectorized fallback: process in chunks with np.where and a small Python loop over chunk boundaries, or ship tau=0.5 (vectorized, zero cost) as default and tau>0.5 as the numba-gated high-ratio mode. Decode path is UNCHANGED from P1 (cumsum of k) — dead-zoning is encoder-only, which is the beauty of closed-loop. Add a --tau sweep to scripts/metropt3_rate_distortion.py to trace the Pareto frontier honestly.
proposals.risk: Encoder becomes sequential for tau>0.5: pure-Python fallback at 1.5M x N points is slow (~seconds-to-minutes), so the honest encode-MB/s benchmark takes a hit unless numba is present — report both. Visual artifact changes character: quiet regions become flat gray, which aids anomaly-spotting but hides micro-texture; tau is a user knob so the tradeoff is explicit. Zstd on the raw k grid will beat PNG DEFLATE here; keep PNG as the viewable artifact and report the Zstd container as the headline ratio (both already exist in container.py).
proposals.interactions: Pure multiplier on P1/P2 — requires their closed loop (dead-zoning an OPEN-loop coder would accumulate the dropped residuals and re-create the drift disaster). Synergy with the entropy stage is the whole point. Slight tension with escape coding: bursty channels after a long dead zone can need |k|>127; the escape list already handles it.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Same (n_vars x n_time-1) uint8 grid, same PNG path. The image gets MORE legible for its stated purpose: quiet = uniform 128 gray, events = sharp bright/dark strokes, i.e. compressed-domain anomaly detection by eye gets easier, and per-timestep resolution is untouched (unlike PAA).

proposals.name: P4 — Pure log-domain closed-loop deltas for strictly positive channels (rank 4: purest relative semantics, but re-imports a dispatch heuristic — do as a config of P1, not a code path)
proposals.mechanism: For channels verified strictly positive with bounded dynamic range, use y = ln(x) instead of asinh(x/s) in the P1 machinery: m = round(ln(x)/q), pixel = diff(m)+128. Each integer step is then EXACTLY a fixed multiplicative ratio e^q, so the grid literally is the percent-change grid (k·q ≈ fractional change), and the guarantee is a pure relative bound |x̂/x - 1| <= e^{q/2} - 1 ≈ q/2, the same guarantee class as SZ3's rel mode.
proposals.why_it_wins: Where valid, it is the information-theoretically exact realization of TRACQ's founding intuition (equal codes = equal relative changes) with zero transform distortion at small |x| that asinh's linear region introduces, and it maps 1:1 onto the paper's narrative. But it is strictly a special case: asinh(x/s) → ln(2x/s) + O((s/x)^2) for x >> s, so P1 with s_i <= 0.1·min(x_i) is within a quarter-quantization-step of pure log while remaining total (defined at zero and below). There is no rate-distortion payoff over well-tuned P1 — only narrative clarity.
proposals.expected_gain: Equal to P1 with small s on positive channels (differences under 0.3 bits/px and within the q/2 bound); its value is enabling an SZ3-rel-mode apples-to-apples comparison column in the benchmark tables and a clean theorem statement in the paper. No gain on any channel that touches zero — there it must fall back, which is the problem.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In ClosedLoopGrid, transform='log' branch: validate np.min(x_i) > 0 else raise/fall back to asinh; y = np.log(x); everything downstream identical. ~10 lines. The channel classifier (min > 0 and max/min < 1e12) is 2 lines but IS a heuristic — exactly the class of special-casing P1 exists to abolish, which is why this ranks last on robustness x simplicity despite maximal spirit-fidelity.
proposals.risk: Re-introduces per-channel dispatch logic (the auto_offset smell in new clothes); a deployment-time zero in a 'strictly positive' channel is a hard failure (log(0) = -inf) requiring either the offset hack again or silent fallback. Recommendation: ship only as transform='log' config value for the paper's ablation table, keep asinh-with-small-s as the default that users actually run.
proposals.interactions: Subsumed by P1 (identical code path, different y). Composes with P3 identically. If exposed, document that s-selection in P1 already covers this regime so users are never forced to choose.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Identical grid and PNG path; pixel gray level is exactly quantized log-ratio, the most literal 'relative change image' of all four proposals.

overall_assessment: P1 (closed-loop asinh integer delta grid) is the single proposal that matters most: it removes the root cause of every measured failure — open-loop multiplicative error compounding — by construction rather than by patching, and it simultaneously deletes the epsilon, auto_offset, near_zero_std_factor, clamp-blending, and anchor heuristics (P1 and P2 both eliminate the offset machinery entirely; P4 does not). Verified numerically in this session: the closed loop collapses to k=diff(round(y/q)), is fully vectorizable in numpy with no sequential scan, holds a q/2 error bound over 1.5M steps with zero drift, and yields a zero-centered Laplacian code alphabet at ~4.8 bits/px where the current mu-law output is incompressible. What I would ship: ONE ClosedLoopGrid implementation in tracq/core_enhanced.py exposing the P1 machinery with a per-variable transform-scale knob s_i (small s = P4's pure relative coding, sigma-scale s = P2's affine/absolute coding — both fall out of the same 120 lines), escape-coded 8-bit deltas, per-variable q derived from a user-specified mixed abs/rel error bound (closing the missing-error-bound gap to SZ3/ZFP), plus P3's dead-zone (tau) as the encoder-only rate knob that turns quasi-stationary stretches into near-free zeros. For the RMSE-headline benchmarks, default s_i ≈ sigma_i (absolute-leaning), because RMSE rewards absolute bounds; report the relative-bound operating points separately. Honest expectation: P1 alone moves TRACQ from 'diverges / loses by 3-5 orders' onto ZFP's rate-distortion curve at low rates; P1+P3 is what produces actual Pareto wins (MetroPT-3 ratio ~0.002-0.008 at RMSE <= 1.7 with per-timestep resolution PAA cannot offer). Delete mu-law and anchors-as-accuracy-patch rather than composing with them; keep anchors only as int64 random-access checkpoints.
